body.statement: Each eligible selector-correction, reachable-fixing, labelled-elimination, and residual-compilation transition preserves the represented observation-target relation on its registered branch domain after composing its emitted circuit, and discharges exactly its displayed polynomial identity or inequality obligation. For every nonhalting transition \(\zeta\Rightarrow\zeta'\), \(\mu_H(\zeta')<_{\mathrm{lex}}\mu_H(\zeta)\): selector correction removes one \(\sigma\)-token, fixing removes one active vertex, elimination removes a nonempty active set or one \(\ell\)-token, and residual compilation removes the sole residual token and enters a terminal state. Therefore the deterministic schedule terminates after finitely many encoded transitions, conditional only on the residual verifier finding a candidate.
body.justification: The calculus is executable only when every scheduled move has a decidable eligibility test, an exact successor, and a local invariant.
body.gap: The anchor algorithm names graphical operations but does not provide a fixed-support retained-image transition semantics with a per-rule decreasing certificate.
body.consumer: A selector-aware implementation can reject malformed transitions and replay every certificate from its encoded state log.
body.proof_tex:
Associate to a state the relation between its labelled kernels and the pair \((O_H^N,T_{a,H}^N)\) obtained by recursively evaluating the retained normalized tables subject to \(\mathcal J\).  This relation holds initially by \(\textnormal{thm:normalization-equivalence}\).

For \(\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{sc}}\), the stored multiplexer has status one at its labelled context, so its value is \(x_s\).  Replacing the gate occurrence by \(\mathbf 1\{X=x_s\}\) and substituting \(x_s\) in its children is therefore a polynomial identity under the appended zero-one and coordinate-copy equations.  The only division is the already displayed context normalization by \(p_H(S=s)\).  Thus the invariant and exactly the selector obligations are preserved.

For \(\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{fix}}\), eligibility supplies the reachable-fixing condition and a nonzero margin on the registered domain.  The successor kernel is defined as \(K_{s,D}/m_{s,W}\).  Multiplying by \(m_{s,W}\) recovers the predecessor kernel, and the verifier checks this identity modulo \(\mathcal J\).  Its separate sum-product certificate is exactly the displayed positivity obligation.  Hence no unregistered division is used and the invariant is preserved.

For a sum elimination, finite distributivity gives the emitted identity \(\sum_Z\prod_{k\in L}K_k\).  For a district elimination, the fixed topological quotient gives the unique ordered factorization into proper-district kernels.  In either case the verifier cancels common factors, checks the resulting equality after cross-multiplication, and separately checks every denominator factorization.  These are exactly, and not more than, the obligations in \(\textnormal{def:elimination-transition}\).  A residual projection similarly preserves the target relation by the accepted cross-multiplied target identity.  A residual contrast preserves the two displayed observation maps and separates the target by the accepted polynomial identities and strict sign certificate.  Thus each eligible transition discharges its own stated obligations and preserves the represented relation in the appropriate formula or twin sense.

It remains to prove finiteness.  A selector step leaves \(|R|\) fixed and lowers \(|\Sigma|\) by one.  A fixing step lowers \(|R|\) by one, regardless of changes in later coordinates.  An elimination step either lowers \(|R|\) by the nonzero number \(|Z|\), or leaves the first three coordinates fixed and lowers \(|\mathcal L|\) by one.  A residual step leaves earlier coordinates fixed, lowers \(|\mathcal R|\) from one to zero, and enters a terminal state.  Therefore every admitted nonterminal move strictly lowers
\[
\mu_H=(|R|,|\Sigma|,|\mathcal F|,|\mathcal L|,|\mathcal R|)
\]
in lexicographic order.  Lexicographic order on \(\mathbb N^5\) is well founded: if an infinite decreasing sequence existed, its first coordinate could fall only finitely often, after which the same argument applies successively to coordinates two through five, a contradiction.  Hence no execution has infinitely many admitted transitions.  If the residual verifier accepts a candidate, its transition is the unique scheduled halting move; without such a candidate the finite execution may be stuck, which is exactly the condition retained in the theorem's final clause.
